cohort: 1,342,655 live births in the municipality of São Paulo, Brazil, between 2007 and 2013
finding: The prevalence of low birth weight was 9.65%, and risk factors included young maternal age, absence of a partner, low maternal education, non-white race, preterm birth, twin pregnancy, a low number of prenatal consultations, and cesarean delivery.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was associated with low birth weight.
birth_weight: low birth weight (average of 3234.55 grams in the term group and 2312.17 in the preterm group)
